response.text:
I can’t say I’m “working on it” overnight or continue in the background — I don’t have any automation or a way to keep working after this turn. I also can’t claim progress I haven’t actually made.

If you want this comparison done, here are practical next steps I can do right now (pick one or more):

- Prepare a complete comparison plan and deliverable checklist (what I’ll compare, formats, workflow, timeline, sample CSV/column template).
- Build a comparison template/spreadsheet you can drop data into (recommended columns: contract ID, counterparty, effective date, expiration, renewal terms, termination rights, liability cap, indemnities, governing law, key obligations, payment terms, unusual clauses, risk rating, notes).
- Walk you through an efficient workflow to compare 300 contracts (manual vs automated options, required staffing, tool recommendations, estimated effort ranges).
- Start analysis immediately if you upload a sample set (or a representative sample of 5–10 contracts) and tell me which clauses/fields matter most.

Questions to proceed:
1. Where are the contracts stored and in what format (PDF, Word, scanned images)?
2. Are they substantially similar templates or widely different?
3. Which clauses/fields are highest priority for the comparison?
4. Any confidentiality or processing restrictions?
5. Do you have access to any contract-analysis tools or do you want a manual/Excel-based workflow?

Tell me which option you want and answer the questions you can; I’ll produce the plan/template or begin analysis in this session.
